key_insight: AutoGaze learns to autoregressively 'gaze' at a small, informative set of spatiotemporal patches and removes redundant pixels before a ViT or MLLM, enabling efficient processing of long, high‑resolution videos without large accuracy loss.
problem_solved: Current ViT/MLLM pipelines process every pixel/frame equally, causing excessive compute, memory, and latency on long or high‑resolution videos due to large spatiotemporal redundancy.
method: Lightweight front-end module that autoregressively selects a minimal set of multi-scale spatiotemporal patches (gazes) and filters out redundant patches before the backbone ViT/MLLM.
Training combines next-token prediction with reinforcement learning to trade off task performance and sparsity (compute reduction) and to learn an efficient selection policy.
Design is model-agnostic and compatible with existing ViTs and MLLMs, allowing scalability to longer/higher-resolution video inputs with low overhead.
impact: Enables practitioners to process much longer and higher-resolution videos with substantially lower compute and memory, making multimodal video understanding and retrieval more practical in resource-constrained or real-time settings.

paper_title: Attend Before Attention: Efficient and Scalable Video Understanding via Autoregressive Gazing
paper_authors: Baifeng Shi, Stephanie Fu, Long Lian, Hanrong Ye, David Eigen
